 Mary Walrath-Holdridge USA TODAY Nov. 17, 2026, 5:31 p.m. ET Hear this story The United States Department of Agriculture is warning consumers to stay away from certain breakfast products sold at workplaces and in vending machines.
 In a public health alert issued on Nov. 14, the USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) said several ready-to-eat foods have been impacted by a recall of biscuits made by C.H. Guenther & Son. Products like breakfast sandwiches that use the biscuits could be contaminated with listeria, the agency said.
 Listeria is a harmful bacterium that can cause serious and even fatal illness in some people, including children, older people and pregnant people. While it's most dangerous to certain groups, listeria can sicken anyone, so FSIS advises against eating the affected products.
 The list of products included in the alert is expected to grow. For now, here's what to know.
 Which products are recalled?
 As of Nov. 14, FSIS had only one biscuit product on its health alert. However, it expects to add more recalls as progress. The ready-to-eat biscuits were sold in vending machines in six states, including Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Tennessee and Texas.

 Related products recalled: 
 On Nov. 8, Fresh & Ready Foods recalled 2,414 sausage, egg and cheese sandwiches distributed in break rooms, refrigerated vending machines and cafeterias, as part of the larger biscuit recall.
 Fresh to You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwich: SKU 3100048, UPC 8 405493 0168 4, best by 11/07-11/19.
 What to do with affected biscuits
 Consumers who have the affected product should throw it away and not eat it, according to FSIS.
 Consumers with food safety questions can call the toll-free USDA Meat and Poultry Hotline at 888-MPHotline (888-674-6854) or send a question via email to MPHotline@usda.gov .

See affected product Taylor Farms recalls salad kits sold at H-E-B. See affected product What are the symptoms of listeria poisoning?
 Listeria poisoning , or listerosis, is a foodborne bacterial infection most commonly caused by the bacterium listeria monocytogenes, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). It is considered a serious condition and can be dangerous or life-threatening, especially when contracted by adults over 65, people with weak immune systems and pregnant women.
 Symptoms usually start within two weeks of eating contaminated food, but may begin as early as the same day or as late as 10 weeks after. According to the CDC, symptoms include:
 Fever
 Muscle aches
 Headache
 Stiff neck
 Confusion
 Loss of balance
 Convulsions
 Diarrhea
 Other gastrointestinal symptoms
 Miscarriage, stillbirth, premature delivery and/or life-threatening infection of newborn infants
 Death
 People in higher-risk categories who experience flu-like symptoms within two months of consuming contaminated food should seek medical attention.
